CRI / NOREPINEPHRINE

Norepinephrine CRI

Uses the shared patient weight above. Workbook profiles & clinical references.

Have a replacement syringe ready • Avoid interruption • Monitor catheter site

Prepare an infusion

Choose a compatible syringe with sufficient capacity for the final preparation volume.

Central catheter required for concentrations >16 mcg/mL. This is an application policy. Assess peripheral access and monitor the site at any concentration. The existing 64 mcg/mL application limit still applies.

Changing concentration requires verification of pump settings and the local line-changeover procedure. Residual medication in tubing can delay delivery of the new concentration.

Stock strength · 1 mg/mL by default

Verify the vial label. Enter norepinephrine equivalent strength in mcg/mL.

Editing the pump rate recalculates the delivered dose at the selected concentration.

Duration estimates when the syringe empties at the current rate. It changes with titration. Check preparation expiry separately.

Verify patient weight, stock strength, concentration and pump settings. Use mcg/kg/min mode when supported by the pump and local protocol.

Confirm the prescribed settings before starting an infusion.

Norepinephrine · titration chart

A valid patient preparation is required to generate the chart.

Patient / cage: ____________________

Keep the concentration fixed while titrating to the prescribed goal. The chart gives calculated rates for reference target doses. Confirm actual pump precision and reprint after any input change.

Sources

  • The Hospira label specifies 1 mg/mL of norepinephrine base equivalent, lists 5% dextrose as a diluent, and describes light protection and room-temperature storage for the labeled diluted product. Verify the exact product and follow local pharmacy guidance for the expiry of your syringe preparation. Hospira Levophed labeling, sections 2.3, 3 and 16.
  • The 0.05 mcg/kg/min default is an editable application setting. Confirm the prescribed veterinary dose and titrate to the clinical goal. MSD Veterinary Manual, Monitoring the Critically Ill Small Animal Using the Rule of 20.
  • Extravasation has been documented in dogs and cats receiving norepinephrine CRIs. Monitor the catheter site and follow local administration procedures. Vasquez et al., Journal of Veterinary Emergency and Critical Care, 2025.
